text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"NJ","level":"state","category":"screening_restrictions","status":"in_force","title":"New Jersey Fair Chance in Housing Act (criminal record screening limits)","requirement":"Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record, orally or in writing, or require an application that includes such inquiries, before making a conditional offer. The only exceptions are methamphetamine manufacture on the premises of federally assisted housing, and lifetime sex offender registration. Before or after a conditional offer, providers may not evaluate applicants on arrests or charges without conviction, expunged convictions, pardoned convictions, vacated or nullified convictions, juvenile adjudications, or sealed records. After a conditional offer, only certain convictions may be considered: murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, sexual assault, certain child sexual-act offenses, or any crime resulting in lifetime sex offender registration; first-degree indictable offenses within 6 years; second- or third-degree offenses within 4 years; fourth-degree offenses within 1 year (measured from the conviction or the end of any prison sentence). A conditional offer may be withdrawn only if the provider determines by a preponderance of the evidence that withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest, after an individualized assessment of six factors. The provider must give written notice stating the specific reasons and an opportunity to appeal with evidence of inaccuracy or rehabilitation. Applicants may request the information relied on within 30 days of the withdrawal notice, and the provider must supply it free of charge within 10 days. Before accepting any application fee, the provider must disclose in writing whether criminal history is part of its eligibility criteria and that the applicant may submit evidence of inaccuracy or rehabilitation. Housing advertisements may not state that applicants with arrests or convictions will not be considered. Providers may not require drug or alcohol tests or consent to obtain drug treatment facility information. Criminal records may not be disseminated or used for purposes inconsistent with the act. Enforcement is by complaint to the Division on Civil Rights, with no court action by private parties.","key_value":"Ban on criminal record inquiries before a conditional offer; look-back limits of 6 years (first-degree), 4 years (second/third-degree) and 1 year (fourth-degree) after a conditional offer","coverage_conditions":"Applies to housing providers offering rental dwelling units for residential purposes.","exemptions":"Excludes a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.","coverage_logic":{"covers":null,"exempt":{"all":[{"field":"owner_occupied","op":"==","value":true},{"field":"units","op":"<=","value":4}]}},"subject":"landlord","interaction":null,"yields_to_local":false,"preempts_local":false,"effective_date":"2022-01-01","effective_rule":{"type":"first_day_of_nth_month_after","n":7,"enacted":"2021-06-18"},"enacted_date":"2021-06-18","end_date":null,"penalty":"Civil penalty up to $1,000 for a first violation, up to $5,000 for a second violation within 5 years, and up to $10,000 for two or more other violations within 7 years; the director may also order cease and desist, return of the application fee, up to $1,000 of the penalty paid to the applicant, and remedial offers.","citation":"P.L.2021, c.110 (N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 to 46:8-64)","quoted_span":"A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.","supporting_spans":["This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment,","Approved June 18, 2021."],"confidence":0.95,"conflict_note":null}],"notes":"Only the screening_restrictions category is addressed. The act has no cap on application fees; it only requires a disclosure before an application fee is accepted and lets the director order a fee refund as a remedy. Effective date computed as the first day of the 7th month after enactment on 2021-06-18, giving 2022-01-01."}
